producer_rule.in_words: Yes. The contract (node_kind enum) admits ACCOUNT, SLEEVE, MODEL_WRAPPER (legacy), MODEL_LEAF, SECURITY, CASH, UNRESOLVED, CATEGORY. The serving code in the holdings folder (snapshot.py) builds nothing: it keeps every node whose root account is selected and re-derives totals, so a node the gold runner emits with a value and no security beneath it is served as emitted. The gold runner emits three shapes of that kind. (1) The SmartX-overlay builder gives every account exactly one level-1 sleeve (node_kind CATEGORY since ruling msg 102475; its docstring still calls it SLEEVE): Models, SMA Tax, or Client. When the account's position rows do not tie to net_mv_positions within the tolerance, or a market value is null, the drill is WITHHELD: the sleeve is carried at the account's balance value, `continue` skips every child, and the sleeve gets a 'DRILL WITHHELD' capability fact; a test asserts the sleeve has no children. (2) A Client or SMA Tax sleeve of an account with no position rows gets one CASH child only. A Models sleeve's MODEL_LEAF holds TARGET-basis SECURITY nodes plus a CASH node; with no model positions only the CASH node. (3) In the Eclipse-overlay builder a node_kind SLEEVE (':managed') is emitted with a value and a MODEL_LEAF child only, never a security. The producer marks a hole only through the 'DRILL WITHHELD' fact; the served class_totals_remainder block is the contract's carrier for custody value with no actual position under it (a model sleeve whose holdings are not observed, a withheld drill). Securities under a Models sleeve are basis TARGET, and the aggregates exclude TARGET (snapshot.py:261).
